The assessee holding shares of a Bombay company supports the argument's reference to the shares as situated in British India.
Holding shares in the Bombay company triggers the application of the accrual of income concept to those shares.
The specific dividend income of Rs. 47,120 triggers the issue concerning its place of accrual.
The company's residence in British India supports the argument's claim regarding the shares being an asset linked to British India for accrual purposes.
The company being resident in British India satisfies the condition in the concept for accrual of dividend from shares in a British India company.
Profits kept in Baroda partially satisfy the scenario in the concept but are overridden by the 'despite' clause for accrual in British India.
